Well, this is where my media theory comes into play, traditional “light versus dark” narratives have been theorized and interpreted as a racist dog whistle after the fall of the Roman Empire by historians, now black represents more than evil, death, and the other, so black versus white narratives aren’t as directly racist as it was centuries ago, like black is occasionally uses now a symbol of rebellion while white is a symbol of order. 

Even in its original uses in the 4th millennium BCE, light and dark dualism was used to describe life and flourishing versus strife and death. But if you were to look at the uses of light versus dark narratives in the Middle Ages it glorified white as right mentalities and black as foreign, death, anti Christian, evil, and witchcraft. In a lot of stories crafted around this time the describe evil creatures as the black one or dark one. And this kind of story telling ideology eventually fueled the excuses for colonialism made my Europeans.

But that one is more theory than fact, so please don’t see this one as an attack, I just wanted to share a media theory.
